newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia stands by warning on Busang - official.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia stands by warning on Busang - official.

text.p: Indonesia is prepared to take control of the huge Busang gold find if Canadian firms Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp fail to settle with their local partners, a ministry official confirmed on Thursday.

He said an explicit warning to this effect had been contained in a letter to be sent to the companies on January 17, giving them a month to come to an agreement with their partners, but had been deleted before actual dispatch because it was "too strong".
Nevertheless, the official said on Thursday: "The spirit of the letter is clear.
"If they fail, to whom will the management of Busang go? It will certainly go to the government because we are a sovereign country and we manage our land.
"The government will find other qualified investors if they (Bre-X and Barrick) fail to settle (with their local partners)."

The official, who declined to be identified, is close to the Busang negotiations. He said the mining ministry's secretary-general Umar Said had deleted the latter part of the sentence containing the warning in the final letter because it was "too strong".

Reuters on Monday obtained a copy of the letter, which a senior source involved in the negotiations said had been sent to Bre-X and Barrick giving them a month from January 17 to sort out their relationships with their Indonesian partners.

A sentence in that letter stated: "If in that one month that agreement mentioned is not achieved, then everything that had been discussed previously will be cancelled, and the government will have the full right to manage Busang II and III."
Bre-X spokesman Steve McAnulty said in Toronto on Tuesday the letter the company received did not contain the words "and the government will have the full right to manage Busang II and III".
The government has still not awarded the contracts of work required to further explore and develop Busang II and III. Bre-X has a contract of work for Busang I.

Bre-X and Barrick made a submission to the government last month outlining their agreement to jointly develop the find, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold worth over $21 billion at current prices.
The submission from the Canadian firms said Bre-X would take a 22.5 percent stake in the Busang property and Barrick 67.5 percent. The government would own the remaining 10 percent.
The government letter on January 17 was in reply to the submission by Bre-X and Barrick.
The Indonesian ministry official said on Thursday there were potential foreign investors who had shown interest in Busang, but he declined to give details.
Canada's Placer Dome Inc made a $5.0 billion merger offer to Bre-X last week.
Complicating the issue is a C$2.0 billion (US$1.48 billion) lawsuit filed in Canada last week by Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh, who claims 40 percent of the Busang find.
Merukh has a 10 percent interest in the Busang I area, the poorest in gold of the three adjoining Busang areas.

Bre-X late last year announced a deal with PT Panutan Duta, controlled by President Suharto's eldest son, Sigit Harjojudanto, under which the company would receive $1.0 million a month for 40 months and a share of the Busang find when Bre-X received a contract of work.
Barrick is involved with the Citra Group, controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana.
Indonesian timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hassan, a close associate of Suharto, was also reported this week to have bought into PT Askatindo Karya Minerals with a stake in Busang.
